title: Pacing latency grokker — annotated mini‑bench notes
body:
Purpose:
Short notes from a quick lab to 'grok' how pacing multipliers change the latency-cost tradeoff under microbursty arrival patterns. This is an engineers' scratchpad — rough numbers, ascii charts, open questions at the end. Goal is a small actionable checklist for the console heuristics team and an input for the pacing-knobs UI copy.

Context / why this run: 
- Product ask: better default pacing multiplier per SLO tier so small-session apps get lower p99 without blowing dollars.
- Hypothesis: intermediate pacing multipliers (0.6–0.8) can reduce p99 significantly for bursty arrivals by smoothing scheduling while preserving >85% of batching savings vs conservative (0.95) settings.

Benchmark setup:
- Hardware: 4x A100 logical pools (p99-oriented profile).
- Model: fast-llm-7B quantized (representative for chat microsessions).
- Workload: Poisson baseline + injected microbursts (5s bursts every 60s) with 200–800 concurrent sessions within bursts.
- Key metrics: p50, p95, p99 (ms), throughput (tokens/s), USD per 1M tokens (cost estimate from internal pricing model).
- Duration: 90 minutes per tuning, repeated 3x to get variance.

Tuning variants (names used in code):
- aggressive (pacing=0.4) -> favors batch fullness, accepts higher queuing delay
- moderate (pacing=0.7) -> balance; our targeted sweetspot in hypothesis
- conservative (pacing=0.95) -> low queuing, more immediate dispatch, lower batch efficiency

Representative aggregated results (median of runs):
+----------------+---------+---------+---------+-----------------+
| variant        | p95(ms)| p99(ms)| tokens/s| $ per 1M tokens |
+----------------+---------+---------+---------+-----------------+
| aggressive     | 120     | 450     | 38k     | $9.6            |
| moderate       | 85      | 200     | 33k     | $10.5           |
| conservative   | 60      | 120     | 27k     | $12.8           |
+----------------+---------+---------+---------+-----------------+

Notes on the table: costs are model+infra blended (includes small amortized idle), tokens/s is sustained throughput under bursts. aggressive gets best tokens/s (big batches) but p99 explodes during microbursts due to head-of-line queueing. conservative minimizes p99 but reduces batching efficiency and increases amortized dollars per token.

Simple ascii visual: p99 vs cost tradeoff (x axis cost relative, y axis p99).

   p99 (ms)
   500 +                    * aggressive
       |
   300 +            * moderate
       |
   150 +         *
       |      * conservative
    50 +
       +-------------------------------
        $9     $10     $11     $12     $13

Interpretation / takeaways:
1) Moderate pacing (0.65–0.75) offers a strong middle path: ~55% p99 improvement vs aggressive while only increasing cost ~10%. For most interactive apps that desire reasonable p99 (<250ms) at bounded cost, this seems like a good default.
2) If the product is ultra-latency-sensitive (p99 < 120ms required), conservative pacing is the only safe option — expect ~20–30% higher unit cost in these microburst scenarios.
3) Aggressive pacing is valuable for throughput-first workloads (batch inference, embeddings pipelines) but harmful for micro-burst interactive workloads: p95 looks OK but p99 spikes.
4) Variance matters: during the largest bursts (>600 sessions) aggressive p99 had long tails (1–2s) for 2–5% of requests — this is noticeable in UX and causes retries.

Latency breakdown (approx median sample from moderate run, numbers in ms):
- scheduling delay (time waiting for batch slot): 35
- network transfer + handshake: 12
- decode (model): 28
- tail amplification (scheduler reorder/priority churn): 10
- total p95 ~85, p99 ~200

Operational heuristics suggested:
- Default pacing per SLO tier:
  - realtime-high (p99 target <= 120ms): pacing=0.92–0.98, disable opportunistic tiling
  - realtime-medium (p99 target <= 250ms): pacing=0.65–0.75, enable aggressive KV prefetch but keep small-session penalty cap
  - throughput (non-interactive): pacing=0.35–0.5, allow longer queue windows

- Auto-adaptive rule sketch (pseudo):
  - monitor session interarrival CV (coefficient of variation) and short-window p99
  - if CV > 1.5 and short-window p99 climbing > 2x baseline -> raise pacing by +0.1 (cap 0.95)
  - if sustained low CV < 0.6 and queue fullness < 30% -> lower pacing by -0.15 (floor 0.35)

Quick chart: session CV vs recommended pacing (guide):
CV  | 0.3  0.6  1.0  1.6  2.5
Pace |0.4   0.6  0.7  0.9  0.95
(note: this is a heuristic, tune per-region/hardware)

Open questions / follow-ups (TODOs):
- Repeat with different model families (decoder-only 13B, encoder-decoder for multimodal) — batching shapes differ and decoder cost dominates. (JIRA-OPT-1427)
- Measure user-perceived latency (first-token vs full-response) for chat apps with streaming enabled; streaming handshake cost interacts with pacing in non-obvious ways.
- Add controlled disruption: simulate region failover and see whether conservative pacing reduces survivor-region p99 inflation.
- Safety cap: if autoscaler is actively adding capacity, pacing adjustments should be damped to avoid oscillation. Add hysteresis.

Draft console copy (for UI tooltip on pacing slider):
"Pacing controls how long the system will wait to assemble work into larger batches. Lower pacing increases throughput and reduces cost but can increase the worst-case latency during sudden bursts. Choose higher pacing if you need more consistent p99 latency (good for interactive experiences)."

Small implementation notes for console team:
- Expose pacing as slider with labeled anchors: "Throughput-first" (0.4), "Balanced" (0.7), "Low-latency" (0.95).
- Surface an estimated cost delta and p99 estimate for the customer's recent traffic profile (we can calculate with a short window probe: 5 min).
- Add an "Auto" mode (uses session CV rule above) with small explainer and ability to pin.

Raw logs pointers (internal):
- s3://redwood-bench/pacing-grokker/2029-06-04/run-1/trace.json.gz
- s3://redwood-bench/pacing-grokker/2029-06-04/run-2/trace.json.gz

Immediate next steps (owner: Aisha):
- Share this scratchpad with Product-Optimize for review (Lena).
- Schedule 30m sync with infra-metrics to validate cost model pricing for token-dollar numbers (Samir).
- Start a short canary (48h) with pacing=0.72 for "realtime-medium" tenants flagged by usage tags; collect p99, cost deltas.

End of scratchpad.
